findings.reason: The diff removes `z` from replaceTilde, so `~1.2` and `~1` now produce `>=1.2.0` and `>=1.0.0` with no `-0` lower bound, even under includePrerelease. replaceCaret at classes/range.js:347 still applies `-0`, and README.md:331-332 still says `~1.2` is the same as `1.2.x` and `~1` is the same as `1.x`. So `1.2.0-pre` now matches `1.2.x` but not `~1.2`.
findings.claim: Under includePrerelease, partial tilde ranges (`~1`, `~1.2`) no longer match prereleases of their lowest version. This breaks their documented equivalence to x-ranges.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `const z = options.includePrerelease ? '-0' : ''` and changes `>=${M}.${m}.0${z}` to `>=${M}.${m}.0` (line 312) and `>=${M}.0.0${z}` to `>=${M}.0.0` (line 309). The deleted comment gave the reason for the bound: "this keeps `~1.2` equivalent to the `1.2.x` x-range it's documented as". `replaceCaret` (line 347) still applies `z`, and README.md:331-332 still says `~1.2` is "Same as `1.2.x`" and `~1` is "Same as `1.x`". range-include.js:113 expects `['1.1.x', '1.1.0-a', { includePrerelease: true }]` to match, but the same version would now be rejected by `~1.1`.

findings.reason: No fixture under test/ pairs a `~` range with includePrerelease (a grep for that pattern found nothing), so the locked tests pass with or without the `-0` bound and can't catch the C1/X1 regression. This is a coverage gap rather than a defect of its own, so I lowered it to low.
findings.claim: No locked test covers a tilde range with includePrerelease, so the regression passes as a green build.
findings.evidence: Every `includePrerelease` fixture in range-include.js, range-exclude.js and range-parse.js uses x-ranges, carets, hyphen ranges or comparators. None uses `~` (for example, none of `['~1.1', '1.1.0-a', { includePrerelease: true }]` or `['~1.2', '>=1.2.0-0 <1.3.0-0', { includePrerelease: true }]` exists). The tilde fixtures at range-include.js:60-88 and range-parse.js:53-59 all use the default options.
